ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: Figure I is a large square, with a vertical line in the middle connecting the midpoints of the upper side and the lower side, and also a diagonal line from the lower-left corner to the upper-right corner; the shading is divided into two triangles, respectively at the lower left and the upper right. Figure II is a large square, divided by the horizontal and vertical midlines into four identical small squares, with the upper-left small square shaded gray. Figure III is a large square of a rhombus grid formed by diagonal lines, with one shaded rhombus on each of the left and right in the middle row. Then reason: Let the side length of each large square be 1. In I, the vertical midline intersects the diagonal line at the center of the square; the two right-angle sides of each of the two shaded right triangles are both 1/2, so the area of each is (1/2·1/2)/2 = 1/8, and the total shaded area is 1/4. In II, the shading is a 1/2×1/2 small square, with area 1/4. In III, the horizontal diagonal and vertical diagonal of each shaded rhombus are both determined by the midpoints of the sides and the grid intersection points, and each length is 1/2, so the area of each rhombus is (1/2·1/2)/2 = 1/8, and the two together total 1/4. Therefore the shaded areas of I, II, and III are equal.

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: Figure I is a large square, with a vertical line in the middle connecting the midpoints of the upper side and the lower side, and also a diagonal line from the lower-left corner to the upper-right corner; the shading is divided into two triangles, respectively at the lower left and the upper right. Figure II is a large square, divided by the horizontal and vertical midlines into four identical small squares, with the upper-left small square shaded gray. Figure III is a large square of a rhombus grid formed by diagonal lines, with one shaded rhombus on each of the left and right in the middle row. Then reason: Let the side length of each large square be 1. In I, the vertical midline intersects the diagonal line at the center of the square; the two right-angle sides of each of the two shaded right triangles are both 1/2, so the area of each is (1/2·1/2)/2 = 1/8, and the total shaded area is 1/4. In II, the shading is a 1/2×1/2 small square, with area 1/4. In III, the horizontal diagonal and vertical diagonal of each shaded rhombus are both determined by the midpoints of the sides and the grid intersection points, and each length is 1/2, so the area of each rhombus is (1/2·1/2)/2 = 1/8, and the two together total 1/4. Therefore the shaded areas of I, II, and III are equal.
